# Resume bullets

<!-- Generated by `python run_pipeline.py report` from reports/templates/resume_bullets.md. Edit the template, not this file. -->

Built only from results the pipeline produced. Re-rendered on every build, so they stay true if the data changes.

- Built a reproducible, one-command analytics pipeline (Python, DuckDB SQL, Power BI; 200+ automated tests) that ingests 12 months of portfolio disclosures from 17 AMCs in 17 different Excel layouts, 24 months of daily NAVs and AMFI expense-ratio data for 32 Indian large-cap funds, with every fund-month reconciled to the source file's stated total.
- Measured active share against a Nifty 100 proxy and found 10 of 17 funds, holding 68% of the group's regular-plan assets, below 0.40; their investors pay 1.10 percentage points a year (about ₹1,783 crore a year) above an index fund for portfolios that overlap the index by roughly two-thirds.
- Showed that the textbook 60% closet-indexing threshold flags 16 of 17 funds under SEBI's 80%-in-top-100 rule, derived a 0.40 threshold from a 30-variant sensitivity analysis, and recommended a fee-disclosure flag instead of drops after finding that 9 of the 10 low-active-share funds still beat the index after fees and only 1 of 17 excess returns was statistically significant.

## Do not claim

- That closet indexers underperform. In this window they mostly did not.
- That ₹1,783 crore was "lost" or "saved". It is a fee gap at one quarter's assets.
- That the result is predictive. It covers 12 months of holdings and 24 months of returns.
- Coverage of the whole category by count: 17 of 32 eligible funds were classified (95.6% of regular-plan assets).
